newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks to fail if can't pay higher rates -- LDP.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks to fail if can't pay higher rates -- LDP.

text.p: Japanese banks must raise interest rates to attract customers, and those which cannot afford to pay higher rates will go bankrupt, Koichi Kato, secretary-general of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), was quoted by QUICK electronic information service as saying on Tuesday.
Kato was quoted as saying in a speech that Japanese savings, which now total 1,200 trillion yen, would flee Japan if interest rates were to be kept at the current low levels.
"Financial institutions must raise interest rates in the future. Those which cannot afford to pay (higher) rates will go bankrupt," Kato was quoted as saying.
The interest rate on deposits is 0.3 percent in Japan, while equivalent rates are at least three percent abroad, QUICK quoted him as saying.
